lead.headline: Oʻahu power restoration advances; about 440 customers remained out at 6:30 a.m.
lead.summary: Hawaiian Electric says crews restored another 1,060 Oʻahu customers overnight after Hurricane Lowell, leaving about 440 customers without power as of 6:30 a.m. Wednesday, mainly in Mākaha Valley and pockets of Honolulu and Windward Oʻahu.
lead.why_it_matters: The update shows substantial progress in Oʻahu recovery while giving remaining affected households a current utility estimate and practical restoration guidance.
body: Oʻahu’s post-Lowell power restoration moved substantially closer to completion Wednesday morning. Hawaiian Electric reported that crews restored electricity overnight to another 1,060 customers affected by Hurricane Lowell. As of 6:30 a.m. Wednesday, about 440 customers remained without power, primarily in Mākaha Valley and in smaller pockets of Honolulu and Windward Oʻahu.

The latest utility update is a major improvement from Tuesday night, when Hawaiian Electric reported roughly 1,500 Oʻahu customers still without service. Crews had already completed assessments and most repairs in West Oʻahu, including Nānākuli, Waiʻanae and Mākaha, after access improved. The company said assessments and repairs for the remaining affected areas were expected to be completed later Wednesday.

Restoration does not necessarily mean every individual property can be reconnected immediately. Hawaiian Electric cautioned that some customers may have damage to privately owned electrical equipment. Depending on the damage, a licensed electrician may need to make repairs before the utility can safely restore service to a home or business.

Customers who remain without electricity are advised by Hawaiian Electric to check their main circuit breaker before reporting an outage. Oʻahu customers can use the company’s online outage reporting service or contact the Oʻahu Trouble Line at 1-855-304-1212. Residents should continue to avoid damaged electrical equipment and treat any downed power line as dangerous.

The numbers are a snapshot and can change as crews complete repairs or identify additional localized damage. For PinoyLink Hawaiʻi readers, the practical takeaway is that most storm-related Oʻahu outages have been restored, while a smaller number of customers may still need utility or property-level repairs before service returns.

stories.headline: Manny Pacquiao takes Cabinet-level anti-poverty post
stories.summary: Former senator Manny Pacquiao has taken his oath as Secretary and Lead Convenor of the National Anti-Poverty Commission, returning to Philippine government service in a Cabinet-level role.
stories.why_it_matters: NAPC coordinates and advises on national poverty-reduction and social-reform programs, making the leadership change relevant to Filipino families following government assistance and development policy.
stories.source_name: Philippine News Agency / Presidential Communications Office
body: Former senator and boxing champion Manny Pacquiao has returned to Philippine government service as Secretary and Lead Convenor of the National Anti-Poverty Commission. Pacquiao took his oath before President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. at Malacañang on Tuesday, September 8, according to the Philippine News Agency and the Presidential Communications Office.

The appointment places Pacquiao at the head of the NAPC secretariat with Cabinet rank under Republic Act No. 8425, the Social Reform and Poverty Alleviation Act. He succeeds Lope Santos III. The commission serves as a coordinating and advisory body for the government’s social-reform and poverty-alleviation agenda rather than functioning as a stand-alone benefits program.

NAPC’s mandate includes coordinating anti-poverty programs among national agencies, local governments and the private sector; monitoring implementation; recommending policy measures; and helping basic sectors participate in policymaking. The commission also works on the National Anti-Poverty Action Agenda, which provides a framework for government interventions across social, economic, ecological and governance dimensions.

Pacquiao’s appointment marks his first government post since his Senate term ended in June 2022. He previously served six years in the Senate and earlier represented Sarangani in the House of Representatives. His new role shifts his public-service focus toward coordination of poverty-reduction and social-reform policy.

For Filipinos in Hawaiʻi with family members in the Philippines, the immediate significance is institutional rather than a new individual entitlement: the appointment changes the leadership of the national body that coordinates poverty-alleviation strategy. Any future program, eligibility or assistance changes should be verified through the responsible Philippine government agency before families act on them.
